detailed_rationale:
Heritage Foods is a South-India-focused dairy processor (2.78 million litres/day capacity, 418 SKUs) plus a smaller retail arm. Dairy is structurally a thin-margin, commodity-input business: FY26 sales were Rs.4,526 Cr but net profit was only Rs.150 Cr, an operating margin of 6%, and the quarterly trend is deteriorating rather than improving -- Q2 FY26 OPM was 7%, Q3 FY26 6%, and Q4 FY26 slipped to 4.6%. Milk procurement cost is the classic dairy margin swing factor (processors cannot always pass through raw-milk price hikes to the shelf immediately), and the Q4 compression is consistent with that dynamic rather than a one-off. Revenue growth itself is respectable (11.8% 3-yr CAGR, 11.5% 1-yr) but not enough to offset the margin trend.

One-off item: Other Income spiked to Rs.15 Cr in Q2 FY26 versus a typical Rs.6-8 Cr run-rate, before normalizing back to Rs.6 Cr in Q4 -- a real but modest distortion, already excluded from the margin read above. Balance sheet is fine (D/E 0.33, interest cover ~14.8x), and the company is diversifying into value-added foods, having taken its stake in Peanutbutter & Jelly Limited to 71% (July 2026) -- a legitimate adjacency play, though it adds integration/execution risk on top of the core dairy business. CRISIL assigned an ESG score of 59 in July 2026, a middling, unremarkable rating.

Reverse-DCF: a P/E of ~23-24x for a 6%-margin, ~11-12%-growth dairy business with a deteriorating quarterly margin trend is not undemanding. To earn that multiple the business needs either margin recovery or growth acceleration, and there is no visible catalyst for either in the data reviewed -- if anything, the trend is the opposite (margin compression into Q4 FY26).
recommendation_rationale: The quant score already flags this as a Sell on the 1-year view (Hold on 3-year), and the fundamentals corroborate the more cautious read: real margin compression into the most recent quarter, in a business with structurally thin margins and input-cost exposure it does not control, at a valuation (~23-24x) that isn't obviously cheap for that risk profile. Nothing in the qualitative research supports rescuing this to a flat Hold.
summary: Heritage Foods is a South India dairy processor. FY26 revenue grew to Rs.4,526 Cr, but the operating margin -- always thin in dairy -- compressed further to 4.6% in the most recent quarter from 7% two quarters earlier, driven by raw milk cost pressure that the company could not fully pass through. The stock trades around 23-24 times earnings, which is a full price for a low-single-digit-margin commodity business showing margin pressure rather than margin expansion. We do not see a case for holding this above a Sell rating at current levels.
positive_para: Revenue growth is respectable at 11-12% both on a 3-year and 1-year basis, the balance sheet is conservatively run (D/E 0.33, interest cover ~14.8x), and the company is diversifying into higher-margin value-added foods (Peanutbutter & Jelly Limited, now 71%-owned) which could lift the margin profile over time if executed well.
negative_para: Operating margin has compressed from 7% (Q2 FY26) to 4.6% (Q4 FY26), the most recent print in the series -- a real deterioration, not a rounding effect, in a business that already operates on wafer-thin dairy margins with no pricing power over its principal input (raw milk). At ~23-24x earnings, the market is not pricing in this margin risk; a continuation of the Q4 trend would make the current multiple look expensive rather than fair.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~23-24x earnings for an ~11-12%-growth, single-digit-margin dairy processor with a margin trend that is currently compressing, the multiple prices in stability the recent quarter does not support. Rich relative to the demonstrated earnings power.
